title: Diversity of Matter: Application and Analysis
topic: Exploring Diversity of Matter by its Chemical Composition
subject: Science

questions.question: Substance X conducts electricity and is shiny. Substance Y does not conduct electricity and is dull. Which is likely a metal?
questions.explanation: Metals are typically shiny and good conductors of electricity. Non-metals are typically dull and poor conductors.

questions.question: A substance breaks down into two simpler substances when heated strongly. Is it an element or a compound?
questions.explanation: Compounds can be broken down into simpler substances (elements) by chemical means like heating. Elements cannot be broken down further.

questions.question: Substance A and Substance B are mixed. They retain their original properties and can be separated easily. Is this a compound or mixture?
questions.explanation: In mixtures, constituents retain their original properties and can be separated by physical means. In compounds, properties change and separation requires chemical means.

questions.question: Element Z is found on the far right side of the Periodic Table. Is it likely a metal or non-metal?
questions.explanation: Non-metals are mostly located on the right side of the Periodic Table. Metals are on the left and centre.

questions.question: Why is copper used for electrical wires?
options: It is a good conductor of electricity
It is a poor conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and a very good conductor of electricity, making it suitable for wires.

questions.question: Why is plastic used to cover electrical wires?
options: It is a poor conductor of electricity (insulator)
questions.explanation: Plastic is a non-metal and a poor conductor of electricity (insulator), which prevents electric shocks.

questions.question: Water (H2O) has different properties from hydrogen and oxygen. What does this tell us about water?
questions.explanation: Compounds have different properties from their constituent elements. Mixtures retain the properties of their constituents.

questions.question: In air, oxygen retains its property of supporting combustion. What does this tell us about air?
questions.explanation: Since oxygen retains its properties in air, the components are not chemically combined. This indicates air is a mixture.

questions.question: Diagram P shows only one type of atom. Diagram Q shows two types of atoms chemically bonded. What are P and Q?
questions.explanation: Elements contain only one type of atom. Compounds contain two or more types of atoms chemically bonded.

questions.question: Diagram R shows two types of atoms mixed together but not bonded. What is R?
questions.explanation: A mixture contains different types of atoms or molecules that are not chemically bonded together.

questions.question: Why is carbon dioxide classified as a compound?
options: It contains carbon and oxygen chemically combined
It is found in the air
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a compound because it consists of carbon and oxygen atoms chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

questions.question: Why is steel classified as a mixture (alloy)?
options: It is made of iron and carbon not chemically combined
questions.explanation: Steel is a mixture of iron and carbon (and other elements) where the components are not chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

questions.question: Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have...
options: The same state at room temperature
questions.explanation: Elements in the same group (vertical column) have similar chemical properties due to similar arrangement of outer electrons (conceptually).

questions.question: Can a compound be separated into its elements by physical means (e.g. filtering)?
options: Only if it is a gas
questions.explanation: Compounds are chemically combined and cannot be separated by physical means. Chemical reactions are needed to break the bonds.

questions.question: Can a mixture be separated into its components by physical means?
options: Yes, because they are not chemically combined
Only if it is a solid
Only if it is a liquid
questions.explanation: Mixtures can be separated by physical means because the components are not chemically bonded.

questions.question: A cooking pot has a metal base. Why?
options: Metal is a poor conductor of heat
Metal is a good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat, allowing thermal energy to transfer quickly from the stove to the food.

questions.question: A cooking pot has a plastic handle. Why?
options: Plastic is a good conductor of heat
Plastic is a poor conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat (insulator), preventing the handle from getting too hot to hold.

questions.question: Iron burns in oxygen to form iron oxide. Is iron oxide an element, compound or mixture?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide is formed by the chemical combination of iron and oxygen, making it a compound.

questions.question: Sugar is dissolved in water. The sugar can be recovered by evaporation. Is this a physical or chemical change?
questions.explanation: Dissolving sugar in water forms a mixture. The sugar can be recovered by physical means (evaporation), indicating no chemical reaction occurred.

questions.question: Substance K conducts electricity. Substance L does not. Substance M conducts only when molten. Which is likely a non-metal element?
questions.explanation: Non-metal elements are typically poor conductors of electricity in all states. Metals conduct in solid and molten states. Ionic compounds conduct only when molten/dissolved.
